FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Pavement markings steer and regulate traffic like signs do, appearing alone or beside signs and signals [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
White lines divide lanes flowing the same way, while yellow lines divide opposing traffic [A01].
Why it matters: color alone tells you whether oncoming cars share your road.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Where a solid yellow line runs beside a dashed one, the solid side may not pass while the dashed side may pass when safe [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Yield lines are white triangles in a row aimed at oncoming drivers, marking where to yield for yield and yield-here-to-pedestrian signs [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
When a sign or signal demands a stop, halt ahead of the stop line or the crosswalk, and give way to anyone inside or stepping into the crossing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
Not every crosswalk is painted, so stay alert for pedestrians at intersections with no marked crossing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
Painted lane arrows dictate which moves a lane allows or requires [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A01
Reversible lanes flip direction by time of day, usually between double-dashed yellow lines, so confirm the lane is yours from roadside signs, overhead signs, or special lights before entering [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A01
Over a reversible lane, a green arrow opens the lane below it, a red X closes it, a flashing yellow X limits it to turns, and a steady yellow X orders you out as soon as safety allows [A01].
Why it matters: four indications, four different permissions; the two yellow X forms are the tested pair.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A02
The shared left-turn lane serves left turns from both directions with alternating arrow markings between solid-and-dashed yellow borders; you may enter and wait there but never use it to pass [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A02
Reserved lanes belong to special vehicles by posted signs, often with a white diamond at the roadside or on the pavement; stay out unless you drive a qualifying vehicle, and the handbook's example reserves one for high-occupancy vehicles with two or more aboard [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A02
On multi-lane roads the left lane generally serves passing; with three or more same-direction lanes, cruise in the right or center except to pass, favoring the center when merging traffic is heavy [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A02
Never drive or pass on the shoulder, paved or not, unless a device or official sends you there; other drivers will not expect you and may pull over blindly [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A02
With no turn markings, start from the lane nearest your turn side and finish in the lane nearest your origin, moving directly without crossing lines or blocking traffic, and shift lanes only after the turn [A02].
Why it matters: nearest-to-nearest is the default turn path on unmarked roads.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A03
Bike lanes are roadway slices for cyclists marked by solid white lines with bike symbols and signs, sometimes further split off by double white lines, curbs, posts, or planters [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A03
Where a bike lane runs green, scan for cyclists before crossing the paint and never stop on it [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A03
Drivers may cross a bike lane only to turn, first checking alongside and behind with care [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A03
Sharrows warn drivers that bikes share the lane, promote safe passing, and curb wrong-way riding and door crashes, yet unlike bike lanes they reserve no exclusive space [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A03
Bike boxes are solid-green full-lane-width zones with a cyclist image beside the crosswalk at signalized intersections, giving riders a safe turning pocket [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A03
A pavement detector mark shows cyclists the sweet spot for tripping the traffic signal [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0017]

Misconceptions: white divides same-direction traffic while yellow divides opposing traffic, never the reverse; sharrows grant no exclusive bike space unlike true bike lanes; a flashing yellow X restricts the lane to turning rather than closing it.

Mnemonic: white stays together, yellow keeps apart; solid means stay, dashed means may; green arrows open, red crosses close.

Glossary: reversible lane (a lane whose direction flips by time of day); yield line (a row of white triangles marking where to yield); sharrow (a shared-lane bike marking with no exclusive space); bike box (a green full-width waiting zone for cyclist turns); reserved lane (a lane restricted to special vehicles, often diamond-marked).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every marking rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
